John Harding Lucas II was born on October 31, 1953.
John Harding Lucas II is an American professional basketball coach and former player.
John Harding Lucas II most recently served as an assistant coach for the Houston Rockets of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
John Harding Lucas II attended the University of Maryland where he played basketball and tennis.
John Harding Lucas II was an All-American in basketball at the University of Maryland.
John Harding Lucas II was a Second-team All-American for the Terrapins team in 1973–74.
John Harding Lucas II's teammates were Len Elmore and Tom McMillen during his time as a Second-team All-American.
The Terrapins had a record of 23 wins and 5 losses in the regular season during John Harding Lucas II's 1973–74 basketball career.
The Terrapins had a record of 9 wins and 3 losses in the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) during John Harding Lucas II's 1973–74 basketball career.
The Terrapins lost during the ACC Tournament, which prevented them from going to the NCAA Tournament during John Harding Lucas II's 1973–74 basketball career.
John Harding Lucas II was a First-team All-American in the 1974–75 season.
The Terrapins recorded a 24 wins and 5 losses regular season record during John Harding Lucas II's 1974–75 basketball career.
The Terrapins had a 10 wins and 2 losses ACC record during John Harding Lucas II's 1974–75 basketball career.
The Terrapins won the ACC regular season crown during John Harding Lucas II's 1974–75 basketball career.
The Terrapins lost to NC State in the semifinals of the ACC tournament during John Harding Lucas II's 1974–75 basketball career.
John Harding Lucas II played for the US national team in the 1974 FIBA World Championship and won a bronze medal.
John Harding Lucas II was the first overall pick of the 1976 NBA draft, selected by the Houston Rockets.
John Harding Lucas II was also drafted by the New York Nets of the American Basketball Association.
John Harding Lucas II played in the NBA for fourteen years.
John Harding Lucas II initially played for the Houston Rockets for two years before being awarded to the Golden State Warriors as compensation for signing Rick Barry.
On October 20, 1978, John Harding Lucas II scored a career best 35 points during a 111–108 win over the Trail Blazers while playing for the Golden State Warriors.
John Harding Lucas II missed a series of practice sessions, plane trips and games in his last season with the Golden State Warriors.
The Golden State Warriors suspended John Harding Lucas II and chose not to pick up his contract option during his last season with the Golden State Warriors.
John Harding Lucas II signed with the Washington Bullets as a free agent after being waived by the Golden State Warriors.
John Harding Lucas II continued to miss practices with the Washington Bullets in the 1982–1983 season and admitted he was addicted to cocaine.
John Harding Lucas II entered a rehabilitation program at the beginning of the 1982–1983 season after admitting his addiction to cocaine.
The Washington Bullets waived John Harding Lucas II in 1983.
John Harding Lucas II played professional tennis and minor league basketball before returning to the NBA with the San Antonio Spurs and then moving on to Houston.
John Harding Lucas II's drug problems continued to plague him, leading the Rockets to waive him in 1984 after he underwent rehabilitation.
John Harding Lucas II was reinstated by the Rockets the next season after undergoing rehabilitation.
John Harding Lucas II became a regular season starter for the 1986 Houston Rockets.
John Harding Lucas II failed two drug tests and the Rockets waived him in March before embarking on a playoff run to the 1986 NBA Finals.
John Harding Lucas II was given another chance in January 1987 when he was signed to a ten-day contract by the Milwaukee Bucks, leading to a full contract for the rest of the season.
John Harding Lucas II played four more years in the NBA after signing with the Milwaukee Bucks in 1986–87 and averaged at age 33 a career-high 17.5 points during that season.
On May 8, 1987, John Harding Lucas II scored a team high 30 points to lead the Bucks to an Eastern Conference Semifinals Game 3 win over the Boston Celtics while playing for the Milwaukee Bucks.
The Bucks lost the series in seven games after winning Game 3 against the Boston Celtics.
John Harding Lucas II played more of a reserve role for the next three years after scoring 30 points in Game 3 with the Milwaukee Bucks.
John Harding Lucas II played three games with the Wichita Falls Texans in the Continental Basketball Association (CBA) during the 1991–92 season.

John Harding Lucas II was serving as head coach of the Miami Tropics in the United States Basketball League (USBL) at the time he appeared to help his player, Roy Tarpley, who was scared about making his debut after leaving a drug treatment facility.
John Harding Lucas II returned to the NBA as a coach and eventually became a head coach.
John Harding Lucas II runs a wellness and aftercare substance-abuse recovery program for athletes.
John Harding Lucas II has helped multiple professional athletes with substance abuse, including Freeman Williams, with whom he became close friends.
On August 8, 1991, John Harding Lucas II bought the Miami Tropics franchise of the United States Basketball League to use the team as a tool in helping players overcome drug problems.
John Harding Lucas II only intended to serve as team owner but realized he would be best suited as head coach to help with counselling players.
John Harding Lucas II won two championships in 1992 and 1993 while coaching the Miami Tropics.
John Harding Lucas II decided to step aside after winning two championships with the Miami Tropics.
John Harding Lucas II has coached the San Antonio Spurs, Philadelphia 76ers, and Cleveland Cavaliers for less than two seasons each, compiling a 174–258 overall coaching record.

John Harding Lucas II's most successful stint was with the San Antonio Spurs in 1992–93 where he took over from Jerry Tarkanian (9–11) and went 39–22 the rest of the season, reaching the Western Conference semi-finals.
The next year, the San Antonio Spurs finished 55 wins and 27 losses but lost in the first round of playoffs.
Prior to accepting the head coaching position for the Cleveland Cavaliers, John Harding Lucas II was an assistant coach for the Denver Nuggets for three seasons.
John Harding Lucas II worked with Indiana Pacers guard T. J. Ford in Houston after the guard sustained a neck injury from a hard foul by Atlanta's Al Horford.
John Harding Lucas II was hired as an assistant coach for the Los Angeles Clippers under head coach Mike Dunleavy for the 2009–10 NBA season.
John Harding Lucas II began working with former NFL first round pick JaMarcus Russell in 2010 as a life coach but ceased this role in April 2011.
John Harding Lucas II joined the Houston Rockets as a player development coach in July 2016.
On November 6, 2020, John Harding Lucas II was announced as an assistant in the staff of new Rockets head coach Stephen Silas.
John Harding Lucas II is not only a standout basketball player but also a standout tennis player.
John Harding Lucas II won ACC number one singles championship twice in 1974 and 1976 while at Maryland.
John Harding Lucas II was named the McKelvin Award winner as the conference's top all-around athlete during his time at Maryland.
John Harding Lucas II competed in two Grand Prix tennis tournaments in 1973, another in 1979, and a challenger event in 1979 while playing professional tennis.
John Harding Lucas II reached the semi-finals of the challenger in Raleigh, North Carolina, partnering Fred McNair during his professional tennis career.
John Harding Lucas II won one other tour match by default in doubles in 1973 in Merion, Pennsylvania while partnering Vic Seixas during his professional tennis career.
John Harding Lucas II lost all four singles first round matches which he contested and in straight sets during his professional tennis career.
John Harding Lucas II's best singles result was a 4–6, 4–6 loss to John Austin during his professional tennis career.
John Harding Lucas II's career high ranking was 579th in singles in December 1979 according to the rankings system used at that time.
John Harding Lucas II played World Team Tennis with the San Francisco Golden Gaters in 1976 and the New Orleans Sun Belt Nets in 1978 during his professional tennis career.
John Harding Lucas II and Renée Richards had success teaming up as the Nets' regular mixed-doubles team in 1978 during their World Team Tennis careers.
John Harding Lucas III, John Harding Lucas II's elder son, played college basketball at Oklahoma State and has been a member of several NBA teams.
Jai, John Harding Lucas II's younger son, is currently an assistant coach at Duke University and also played college basketball at the University of Texas.
